title: Progressive SLO Hysteresis and Circuit Tagging for Multi-region Endpoints
creator: Priya Desai
description: Objective: Define and document a new SLO/SLI policy for user-facing endpoints that enables progressive degradation across regions using hysteresis windows, explicit circuit tagging, and error-budget-aware eviction. This ticket captures the SLI definitions, the hysteresis parameters for multi-region soft failover, how circuit breakers will be tagged and scored, and the policy for reallocating error budget when regions are under stress. The goal is to reduce thrash during regional flaps, improve on-call clarity, and make failure modes explorable in the Console.
acceptance_criteria: A concise SLI matrix per endpoint type (chat, streaming, embeddings) with 3 fidelity bands (gold/silver/bronze) and exact measurement formulas
Hysteresis design documented: time windows, backoff ramp rates, and local vs global decision boundaries
Circuit tagging scheme defined so runs, variants, and tenant groups can be scored for preemptive eviction
Error-budget reallocation workflow documented and a PoC automated reallocation policy in staging
Grafana dashboard mockups and alert rules for early-warning probes created and linked
Runbook snippets for on-call that explain how to interpret progressive degradation states
implementation_plan: Draft SLI formulas using request-level attributes (latency P95/P99, token failure rate, quality probe score) — Priya to author draft
Prototype hysteresis controller in a staging region that uses 3-minute and 15-minute windows with decay factors — Rajesh to implement
Create a circuit-tag payload field for the request metadata that is propagated through load balancer and runtime — Marco Nguyen to spec and implement
Add a lightweight error-budget ledger service to track per-endpoint per-region budgets and expose read APIs — Elena Ortiz to design
Integrate dashboard panels and create SLO burn alerts and progressive severity rules in Grafana/Alertmanager
Run chaos experiments (region latency injection) and validate that hysteresis prevents flip-flopping and that the circuit tags appear in traces and logs
updates: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting — aligned on three fidelity bands and the need for hysteresis to be tunable per-route. Action: Priya to produce SLI draft.
2025-01-20: SLI draft posted to Confluence (link below). Early feedback from SRE: include quality probes for generation coherence, not just latency.
2025-01-27: Rajesh prototyped a hysteresis controller that operates on weighted burn rates (alpha=0.3). Initial tests show reduced oscillation in synthetic traffic.
2025-02-02: Design review with Product and Console teams. Decision to expose degradation state in Console as a 4-state enum (Healthy, SoftDegrade, HardDegrade, RegionEjected).
comments: Fatima Khan (SRE): We should ensure the hysteresis windows are configurable per-tenant — enterprise customers will want override knobs.
Jonah Park (Product): Console representation must map to customer-facing SLA pages; avoid exposing internal tokenized states directly.
Marco Nguyen (Infra): Circuit tagging must be compatible with existing tracing headers; propose using x-rw-circuit-tag and a numeric score field.
Elena Ortiz (Observability): The error-budget ledger needs an eventual-consistent model; we should document reconciliation semantics to avoid split-brain budgeting.
decision: Adopt progressive SLO bands with hysteresis windows (3m short, 15m medium, 1h long) and expose degradation states in Console. Circuit tagging will use x-rw-circuit-tag and x-rw-circuit-score headers. Error-budget ledger will be eventual-consistent with periodic reconciliation. The team will iterate parameters based on chaos test results.
risks: Misconfiguration could cause excessive region ejections leading to global capacity pressure
Eventual consistency of the ledger could temporarily misattribute budget and delay reallocation
Customers may misinterpret Console degradation states if not well documented
Instrumentation gaps (missing tags in older runtimes) could yield blind spots during rollouts
metrics: Primary SLOs: availability (successful-response rate) measured per-endpoint AND per-region
Quality SLI: synthetic probe pass-rate (0-100 scale) per minute
Latency SLI: P95 and P99 request-response time including queueing and tokenization overhead
Operational SLI: SLO burn-rate per-region and number of region-ejections triggered per week
Safety metric: percentage of ejections that were reverted within 10 minutes (target < 5% false-ejects)
